ilol-state.t: A minor chiefship of the Mahi Kantha country in northern Gujarat, one of many small Rajput estates.
ilol-state.o: Ilol was one of the petty estates of the Mahi Kantha region, held by a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] family from around 1600. Its founding is known mainly from local tradition.
ilol-state.r: Its Thakor ruled a few villages, paid tribute through the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads]] of [[s:baroda-state|Baroda]] and was supervised by the British Mahi Kantha Agency. Standard works record little else of its history.
ilol-state.e: Ilol was merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in present Sabarkantha district.

imamate-of-futa-jallon.t: A Fulbe Islamic state in the Guinea highlands, created by jihad in the 1720s, which rotated power between two dynasties and was the model for later West African imamates.
imamate-of-futa-jallon.o: Muslim Fulbe pastoralists had moved into the Futa Jallon highlands over several centuries. Around 1725 a [[e:jihad|jihad]] led by the scholar Karamokho Alfa (Ibrahima Sambegu) overthrew the local Jallonke rulers. After his death the warrior Ibrahima Sori completed the conquest in the 1770s and became almamy, building a theocratic state with its capital at Timbo.
imamate-of-futa-jallon.r: The almamy was chosen alternately from two families, the Alfaya descended from Karamokho Alfa and the Soriya from Ibrahima Sori, an arrangement that caused frequent disputes. A council of elders sat at Fugumba, the religious centre, and the land was divided into provinces called diwe. Qur'anic schooling was widespread, and the economy rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]], farming by slaves and trade with the coast at [[e:sierra-leone|Sierra Leone]] and the Rio Pongo.
imamate-of-futa-jallon.e: [[e:france|France]] signed [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] treaties from 1881 and exploited rivalries between the two houses. In 1896 French troops defeated and killed Almamy Bokar Biro at Poredaka, and Futa Jallon was absorbed into [[s:french-guinea|French Guinea]].

iacetani.t: A Pyrenean people of the Jaca valley in Aragon, whose town Iaca is the ancestor of modern Jaca.
iacetani.o: The Iacetani lived in the upper valley of the Aragón river in the central [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]], around modern Jaca, from at least the 5th century BCE. Their affiliation is uncertain: they may have been related to the [[s:vascones|Vascones]] or to the Iberian peoples to the south.
iacetani.r: Strabo places them in the foothills of the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]], and their town Iaca later minted coins with an Iberian legend. They lived from herding and farming in the mountain valleys. Nothing reliable is known of their rulers or institutions.
iacetani.e: They appear among the peoples subdued during Cato's campaign of 195 BCE, though the reference is disputed. Later they lay within [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]], and during the Sertorian war their region was fought over; Iaca survived as a Roman town and gave its name to Jaca.

imperial-abbey-of-salem.t: A wealthy Cistercian abbey near Lake Constance whose abbots ruled one of the largest monastic territories in Swabia.
imperial-abbey-of-salem.o: Salem was founded in the 1130s by the knight Guntram of Adelsreute as a Cistercian house settled by monks from Lucelle. It grew rapidly under Hohenstaufen protection, and in 1354 [[e:charles-iv|Charles IV]] confirmed its direct dependence on the empire. Its status was contested for centuries by [[e:austria|Austria]] and others, but its abbots sat among the prelates of the [[e:imperial-diet|Imperial Diet]].
imperial-abbey-of-salem.r: The abbots ruled a compact territory of villages north of Lake Constance through their own courts and officials, making Salem one of the richest imperial abbeys in Swabia, with vineyards, granges and town houses in [[s:free-imperial-city-of-constance|Konstanz]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-uberlingen|Überlingen]]. Its great Gothic minster dates from around 1300, and the Baroque abbey buildings were rebuilt after a fire in 1697.
imperial-abbey-of-salem.e: In 1802 and 1803 the abbey was secularised and granted to the margraves of Baden, who turned it into Salem Castle, still owned by the family. In 1920 Kurt Hahn and Prince Max of Baden founded the Schule Schloss Salem boarding school there.

indragiri-sultanate.t: A Malay sultanate on the Indragiri River in Riau, Sumatra, that traded pepper and survived under Dutch rule until 1945.
indragiri-sultanate.o: Indragiri's early history is known mostly from local tradition, which dates its founding to 1298 and links its first rulers with the Minangkabau highlands and the Malay courts of the Strait. Its centre lay on the Indragiri River, which carried [[e:pepper|pepper]] and gold from the interior to the sea, with the court eventually settling at Rengat.
indragiri-sultanate.r: Indragiri was a river state whose rulers taxed trade between the upland Minangkabau and the coast. It came under the influence of the [[s:malacca-sultanate|Malacca Sultanate]] and later the [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor Sultanate]], and in the 17th century made [[e:pepper|pepper]] contracts with the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]]. [[e:islam|Islam]] was established at court by the 15th century.
indragiri-sultanate.e: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] extended control in the 19th century, signing treaties that left the sultan a figurehead. The sultanate lasted until [[e:indonesian-independence|Indonesian independence]] in 1945, after which its lands became Indragiri Hulu and Indragiri Hilir regencies in Riau province.

imamate-of-futa-toro.t: A Fulbe Islamic state in the middle Senegal valley, born of a clerical revolution in 1776, which challenged the Atlantic slave trade in Muslims.
imamate-of-futa-toro.o: In the Futa Toro region along the middle [[e:senegal|Senegal]], Torodbe clerics rose in the 1760s and 1770s against the [[s:denianke-kingdom|Denianke Kingdom]] and against raids by Moors from the north. Led first by Sulayman Bal and then by Abdul Kader Kan, they overthrew the Denianke, and in 1776 Abdul Kader became the first almamy of a new Islamic state.
imamate-of-futa-toro.r: The almamy was elected by a council of great Torodbe families, who often deposed rulers they disliked, and he had no fixed capital. The state enforced Islamic law, built mosques and schools, and forbade the sale of Muslims as slaves, demanding that French traders on the river pay tolls and respect this rule. Abdul Kader was killed in 1807 during wars with [[s:kingdom-of-bundu|Bundu]] and [[s:kingdom-of-kaarta|Kaarta]].
imamate-of-futa-toro.e: Weakened by factional rivalry, Futa Toro supplied many followers to Umar Tall, himself a native of the region. Under Faidherbe [[e:france|France]] annexed its western districts around 1859 and divided the rest, and the valley was absorbed into [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]].

ijebu-kingdom.t: Yoruba coastal kingdom east of Lagos whose rulers, the Awujale, grew rich as middlemen between the lagoon ports and the interior.
ijebu-kingdom.o: Ijebu tradition names Obanta as the founder who came from [[s:kingdom-of-ife|Ile-Ife]] and settled at Ijebu-Ode. The area was already densely settled: the vast earthwork known as Sungbo's Eredo, a ditch and bank around 160 km long, was dug around the end of the first millennium. The kingdom took shape by the 15th century.
ijebu-kingdom.r: The Awujale ruled with the Osugbo society of elders, which held judicial power, and with town chiefs. Ijebu controlled routes between the lagoon and the [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] interior and traded cloth, kola and slaves with Europeans on the coast. In the 19th century it profited from the wars between [[s:ibadan|Ibadan]] and its rivals while restricting access to its markets.
ijebu-kingdom.e: When Ijebu closed its roads to [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]] traders, a British force defeated its army at Imagbon in 1892 and occupied Ijebu-Ode. The kingdom was absorbed into British [[e:lagos|Lagos]] and later the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]]. The Awujale still reigns at Ijebu-Ode.

inca-empire.t: The largest empire of the pre-Columbian Americas, Tawantinsuyu stretched some 4,000 km along the Andes, linked by roads and run without money or writing.
inca-empire.o: Around 1438 the ruler of the [[s:kingdom-of-cusco|Kingdom of Cusco]], Pachacuti, defeated the [[s:chanka-confederation|Chanka Confederation]] and launched campaigns of conquest. His son Túpac Inca Yupanqui conquered the [[s:kingdom-of-chimor|Kingdom of Chimor]] and lands from [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Ecuador]] to central [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]], and Huayna Capac extended rule to the north.
inca-empire.r: The Sapa Inca, believed to descend from the sun god Inti, ruled four quarters from Cusco. A road system of some 40,000 km, the Qhapaq Ñan, connected the empire with relay runners and storehouses. Labour tax called [[e:mita|mita]] built terraces, temples and fortresses such as Sacsayhuamán and estates like Machu Picchu. Records were kept on knotted cords called khipus. Quechua was spread as the common language, and conquered peoples were resettled as mitmaq.
inca-empire.e: A civil war between Huáscar and Atahualpa followed Huayna Capac's death, probably from [[e:smallpox|smallpox]]. In 1532 [[e:francisco-pizarro|Francisco Pizarro]] captured Atahualpa at Cajamarca and executed him in 1533. Resistance continued in the [[s:neo-inca-state|Neo-Inca State]], while Quechua and Andean traditions survive today.

inancids.t: A small Turkmen beylik around Denizli (Ladik) in south-western Anatolia, visited by Ibn Battuta.
inancids.o: In the later 13th century, as the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]] weakened, [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] frontier warriors took Ladik, near ancient Laodicea, and the Lycus valley. A local dynasty took shape there under Mehmed Bey and later took its name from Inanc Bey.
inancids.r: Little is known of the [[e:beylik|beylik]]'s government. It lay on the trade road through the Meander valley and produced [[e:cotton|cotton]] textiles embroidered with gold that [[e:ibn-battuta|Ibn Battuta]] admired when he visited Ladik around 1333, describing its ruler as generous. The beylik often depended on the stronger [[s:germiyanids|Germiyanids]] to the north.
inancids.e: Around 1368 the [[s:germiyanids|Germiyanids]] absorbed Ladik, and the region later passed with Germiyan lands to the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]].

isle-of-man.t: A self-governing Crown Dependency in the Irish Sea, with one of the world's oldest continuous parliaments, the Tynwald.
isle-of-man.o: The British crown bought the sovereign rights of the [[s:lordship-of-mann|Lordship of Mann]] from the Duke of Atholl through the Revestment Act of 1765, mainly to stop smuggling that cost the Treasury duties. The island became a direct possession of the crown, though not part of the [[s:united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-ireland|United Kingdom]].
isle-of-man.r: Man kept its own Tynwald, with the elected House of Keys and the Legislative Council, its own laws and taxes. It grew as a Victorian resort, with Douglas as capital from 1869, and hosted internment camps in both world wars. The TT motorcycle races began in 1907. The last native speaker of Manx died in 1974, but the language is being revived.
isle-of-man.e: Since the mid 20th century the Isle of Man has expanded self-government and become an offshore financial centre. It remains a Crown Dependency, with the UK responsible for defence and foreign relations.

ilergetes.t: The leading Iberian people of the Lleida plain, whose chiefs Indibilis and Mandonius switched between Carthage and Rome in the Second Punic War.
ilergetes.o: The Ilergetes occupied the plains of the Segre and Cinca rivers around modern Lleida from the 5th century BCE, with their capital at Iltirta. By the late 3rd century BCE they were among the most powerful peoples of north-eastern [[e:iberia|Iberia]].
ilergetes.r: They were ruled by princes who could raise large armies and dominate neighbouring peoples. Their economy rested on the cereal plains of the Segre, and Iltirta minted coins with an Iberian legend. During the [[e:second-punic-war|Second Punic War]] their leaders Indibilis and Mandonius first served [[e:carthage|Carthage]], then joined Scipio in 209 BCE.
ilergetes.e: In 206 and 205 BCE the brothers revolted against [[e:rome|Rome]]; Indibilis died in battle and Mandonius was handed over and executed. The Ilergetes were absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]], and Iltirta became Roman Ilerda, where Caesar defeated [[e:pompey|Pompey's]] [[e:legatus|legates]] in 49 BCE.

italian-islands-of-the-aegean.t: Italy's Dodecanese colony, seized from the Ottomans in 1912, which left a legacy of Italian architecture before passing to Greece in 1947.
italian-islands-of-the-aegean.o: During the [[e:italo-turkish-war|Italo-Turkish War]] of 1911-1912, [[e:italy|Italy]] occupied [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]] and the other islands of the [[e:dodecanese|Dodecanese]]. The Treaty of Ouchy in 1912 made the occupation provisional, but Italy kept the islands through the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], and the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 recognised its [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]].
italian-islands-of-the-aegean.r: Italian governors ruled from [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]]. Mario Lago (1922-1936) invested in roads, agriculture, archaeology and buildings, including the restored Palace of the Grand Master and new Italian rationalist architecture. His successor Cesare Maria De Vecchi pursued forced Italianisation of education and the [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] church. Many [[e:greeks|Greeks]] emigrated.
italian-islands-of-the-aegean.e: After [[e:italy|Italy's]] [[e:armistice-of-11-november-1918|armistice]] in 1943 German troops took over, defeating the British at Leros and deporting the [[e:jews|Jews]] of [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]] in 1944. British military administration followed in 1945, and the [[e:paris|Paris]] Peace Treaty of 1947 gave the islands to the [[s:kingdom-of-greece|Kingdom of Greece]]; they were formally united in 1948.

indo-greek-kingdom.t: Greek kingdoms in north-western India founded by Alexander's Bactrian heirs, ruled by kings like Menander who mixed Greek and Indian culture.
indo-greek-kingdom.o: Around 180 BCE Demetrius I of the [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Greco-Bactrian Kingdom]] crossed the [[e:hindu-kush|Hindu Kush]] into the [[e:kabul|Kabul]] valley and the [[e:punjab|Punjab]], taking advantage of the fall of the [[s:maurya-empire|Maurya Empire]]. His successors founded a series of Greek-ruled kingdoms in [[s:kingdom-of-gandhara|Gandhara]] and the Punjab, often rivals of one another and of their Bactrian cousins.
indo-greek-kingdom.r: Indo-Greek kings issued bilingual coins with Greek on one side and Prakrit in Kharoshthi on the other, often showing Greek gods beside Indian symbols. Menander I, ruling from Sagala, raided deep into the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges plain]] and appears in the Buddhist text Milindapanha as King Milinda, questioning the monk Nagasena. The envoy Heliodorus, sent by King Antialcidas, set up a pillar to Vasudeva at Vidisha.
indo-greek-kingdom.e: Pressed by [[s:indo-scythians|Indo-Scythians]] and [[s:yuezhi|Yuezhi]] from the north-west, the Indo-Greek kingdoms shrank during the 1st century BCE. The last known king, Strato II, ruled in the eastern [[e:punjab|Punjab]] until around 10. Their artistic legacy fed into the Greco-Buddhist art of [[s:kingdom-of-gandhara|Gandhara]].

islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-pres.t: The restored Taliban state, which took Kabul in August 2021 and has imposed sweeping restrictions on women while seeking international recognition.
islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-pres.o: After a twenty-year insurgency against the [[s:islamic-republic-of-afghanistan|Islamic Republic of Afghanistan]] and NATO forces, and the US withdrawal agreed at Doha in 2020, the Taliban seized [[e:kabul|Kabul]] on 15 August 2021 and restored the Islamic [[e:emirate|Emirate]]. Hibatullah Akhundzada, the movement's leader since 2016, became supreme leader.
islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-pres.r: The supreme leader rules from [[e:kandahar|Kandahar]] by decree, with a caretaker cabinet in [[e:kabul|Kabul]] and no constitution or elections. The regime has banned girls from secondary and higher education and restricted women's work, travel and public life. Foreign aid cuts and frozen assets caused economic collapse and humanitarian crisis, though security improved in many areas. It faces an insurgency by the Islamic State [[e:khorasan|Khorasan]] Province.
islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-pres.e: The Islamic [[e:emirate|Emirate]] remains in power. [[e:russia|Russia]] became the first state to formally recognise it in 2025, while most countries engage with it without recognition.

imagawa-clan-domain.t: The domain of the Imagawa of Suruga, a leading Sengoku power whose ruler Yoshimoto was killed by Oda Nobunaga at Okehazama in 1560.
imagawa-clan-domain.o: The Imagawa, a branch of the Ashikaga, had long been governors of Suruga. After Imagawa Yoshitada died in battle in 1476, a succession dispute was settled with help from Ise Moritoki, later known as Hojo Soun, who secured the domain for the young Ujichika.
imagawa-clan-domain.r: Ujichika expanded into Totomi and issued one of the earliest [[e:sengoku-period|Sengoku]] house codes, the Imagawa kana mokuroku of 1526. His son Yoshimoto made Sunpu a cultured capital, took control of Mikawa, held the young [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] as a hostage and allied with the Takeda and Later Hojo, becoming the strongest lord on the Tokaido.
imagawa-clan-domain.e: Marching west in 1560, Yoshimoto was killed in a surprise attack by [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]] at Okehazama. His son Ujizane lost Sunpu to Takeda Shingen in 1568 and surrendered Kakegawa castle to [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] in 1569, ending the domain.

isin.t: The kingdom founded by a former official of Ur that claimed the Sumerian imperial heritage after 2004 BCE and produced the law code of Lipit-Ishtar.
isin.o: Ishbi-Erra, an official from [[s:mari|Mari]] serving Ibbi-Sin, last king of the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]], made himself independent at Isin around 2017 BCE as Ur's grip failed. After the [[e:elamites|Elamites]] sacked Ur in 2004 BCE, he expelled their garrison and presented his dynasty as the legitimate successor of Ur, controlling [[s:nippur|Nippur]], Ur and [[s:uruk|Uruk]].
isin.r: Isin's kings kept up Sumerian court culture: they wrote royal hymns, copied Sumerian literature and claimed divinity like the kings of Ur. Lipit-Ishtar issued a law code in Sumerian around 1930 BCE. The city goddess Ninisina was a healer, and archaeologists found a cemetery of dogs, her sacred animal. A famous later story tells how Erra-imitti installed a gardener, Enlil-bani, as substitute king, only to die, leaving Enlil-bani on the throne.
isin.e: Isin lost Ur and the Gulf trade to [[s:larsa|Larsa]] around 1932 BCE and became one city-state among several. In 1794 BCE [[e:rim-sin-i|Rim-Sin I]] of [[e:larsa|Larsa]] conquered it. Isin itself revived later, giving its name to the [[s:second-dynasty-of-isin|Second Dynasty of Isin]] in the 12th century BCE.

imperial-abbey-of-weingarten.t: Benedictine abbey founded by the Guelphs that guarded a relic of the Holy Blood and built the largest baroque church in Germany.
imperial-abbey-of-weingarten.o: The Guelph family founded a convent at Altdorf near [[s:free-imperial-city-of-ravensburg|Ravensburg]] in the 11th century and in 1056 replaced it with a Benedictine abbey that became their family monastery. In 1094 Judith of [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]], wife of Welf IV, gave it a relic of the Holy Blood. After the Guelph and Hohenstaufen lines passed, the abbey became imperial, by around 1274.
imperial-abbey-of-weingarten.r: The abbots ruled villages and farmland in Upper Swabia, sat among the Swabian imperial prelates and were among the richest in the region. The Holy Blood relic drew pilgrims, and the Blutritt horseback procession continues today. The Weingarten [[e:manuscript|manuscript]] of medieval German love songs was kept there. From 1715 to 1724 the abbey built its vast baroque basilica.
imperial-abbey-of-weingarten.e: The abbey was secularised in 1803, passing to the house of [[s:principality-of-nassau-diez|Nassau-Orange]] and in 1806 to Württemberg. Benedictine monks returned in the 20th century, and the basilica remains a major pilgrimage church.

inner-austria.t: The Habsburg lands of Styria, Carinthia and Carniola, ruled from Graz, from which Ferdinand II launched the Counter-Reformation across the monarchy.
inner-austria.o: The Treaty of Neuberg of 1379 gave Leopold III the [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] lands south and west of [[e:austria|Austria]], including Styria, Carinthia and Carniola. These duchies were ruled as Inner Austria by Leopold's descendants in the 15th century; Frederick III, who resided at Graz and Wiener Neustadt, later reunited the dynasty's lands. In 1564 Ferdinand I's will recreated Inner Austria for his son Charles II.
inner-austria.r: From Graz the archdukes governed Styria, Carinthia, Carniola, Gorizia and Trieste with their own estates, which were largely Protestant in the 16th century. Inner [[e:austria|Austria]] bore the brunt of Ottoman raids and paid for the Croatian and Slavonian [[s:military-frontier|Military Frontier]]. Charles II founded the University of Graz in 1585 under the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]], and his son Ferdinand expelled Protestant preachers from 1598.
inner-austria.e: In 1619 Archduke Ferdinand became emperor as Ferdinand II, and his Inner Austrian lands merged into the united [[s:habsburg-monarchy|Habsburg Monarchy]], though separate institutions in Graz survived until Maria Theresa's reforms in the 1740s.

indigetes.t: The Iberian people of the Empordà, neighbours of Greek Emporion, whose hill town at Ullastret is the largest Iberian site in Catalonia.
indigetes.o: The Indigetes occupied the Empordà plain of north-east [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] from about the 6th century BCE. Their growth was closely linked with the founding of [[s:emporion|Emporion]] by [[e:greeks|Greeks]] around 575 BCE, and part of their community lived beside the Greek town, which Livy describes as a double city.
indigetes.r: Their largest settlement, at Ullastret, was a walled hill town with towers, temples and grain silos, showing strong Greek influence in its architecture and imports. The Indigetes exchanged grain and other goods for Greek pottery and wine, and minted coins with the Iberian legend Untikesken. Their political organisation was probably based on town elites.
indigetes.e: They took part in the north-eastern revolt against [[e:rome|Rome]] and were subdued by Cato in 195 BCE. Ullastret was abandoned soon afterwards, and the Indigetes merged with the population of Roman [[s:emporion|Emporiae]] and [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]].

iga-confederacy.t: A self-governing league of the small warrior families of Iga province, famous as a home of ninja, crushed by Oda Nobunaga in 1581.
iga-confederacy.o: Iga, a hilly province southeast of [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]], had no strong governor in the [[e:sengoku-period|Sengoku period]]. Its many small landholding warrior families, the jizamurai, formed a league known as the Iga sokoku ikki, and a surviving covenant from around the 1560s sets out its rules.
iga-confederacy.r: The league was governed by councils of local leaders who agreed to defend the province jointly, mobilise all men in emergencies and forbid dealings with outside lords. It cooperated with a similar league in neighbouring Koka. Men of Iga were hired across [[e:japan|Japan]] as specialists in scouting, infiltration and raids, the shinobi, or ninja.
iga-confederacy.e: In 1579 [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga's]] son Nobukatsu invaded Iga and was beaten back. In 1581 Nobunaga sent a large army that overran the province, burned temples and killed much of the population, ending the league's independence.

italian-governorate-of-montenegro.t: Italian-occupied Montenegro in the Second World War, where a planned puppet kingdom was swept away by one of the first mass uprisings in occupied Europe.
italian-governorate-of-montenegro.o: After the conquest of the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]] in April 1941, [[e:italy|Italy]] occupied [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] and planned to restore it as a separate state under Italian protection. On 12 July 1941 an assembly in Cetinje proclaimed the restoration of Montenegro's independence. The next day, 13 July, Communist-led Partisans and other insurgents launched a general uprising that liberated most of the country.
italian-governorate-of-montenegro.r: Italian forces reconquered the towns, and in October 1941 [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] was placed under a military governor, General Alessandro Pirzio Biroli, with harsh reprisals. The occupiers cooperated with Chetnik and separatist groups against the Partisans, and much of the mountainous interior remained a battleground between them.
italian-governorate-of-montenegro.e: When [[e:italy|Italy]] capitulated in September 1943, German forces took over the occupation. The Partisans liberated [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] by December 1944, and it became a republic of the [[s:socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia|Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]]. The 13 July uprising is a Montenegrin national holiday.

iwellemmeden-kel-ataram.t: The western Iwellemmeden Tuareg confederation, which dominated the Niger Bend around Menaka and led a major revolt against the French in 1916.
iwellemmeden-kel-ataram.o: The Iwellemmeden were a [[e:tuareg|Tuareg]] confederation that moved into the region east of the [[e:niger-bend|Niger Bend]] in the 17th century, filling the vacuum after the fall of the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]] and the weakening of the [[s:pashalik-of-timbuktu|Pashalik of Timbuktu]]. In the 18th century they divided into the western Kel Ataram and the eastern [[s:iwellemmeden-kel-dinnik|Iwellemmeden Kel Dinnik]].
iwellemmeden-kel-ataram.r: The Kel Ataram were led by an amenokal, the paramount chief, drawn from a noble lineage. Noble warriors controlled [[e:vassal|vassal]] herders, dependent farmers along the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] and enslaved people. They raided and taxed the Songhai-speaking riverine communities and controlled pastures around Menaka and the Azawagh.
iwellemmeden-kel-ataram.e: [[e:france|France]] occupied the region around 1900. In 1916 the amenokal Firhun ag Alinsar launched a revolt during the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]]; he was defeated and killed later that year, and the confederation's power was broken.

iwellemmeden-kel-dinnik.t: The eastern Iwellemmeden Tuareg confederation around Tahoua, a power on the northern frontier of Hausaland and the Sokoto Caliphate.
iwellemmeden-kel-dinnik.o: The Iwellemmeden confederation split in the 18th century, around 1770, into a western branch, the [[s:iwellemmeden-kel-ataram|Iwellemmeden Kel Ataram]], and an eastern branch, the Kel Dinnik. The Kel Dinnik settled in the Azawagh and the region of Tahoua in present-day [[e:niger-river|Niger]].
iwellemmeden-kel-dinnik.r: Led by an amenokal from a noble lineage, the Kel Dinnik ruled [[e:vassal|vassal]] herding groups and dependent farming villages in the Ader region. They raided and traded with the [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausa kingdoms]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-gobir|Kingdom of Gobir]], and in the 19th century alternately fought and cooperated with the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]]. Salt, livestock and grain were the basis of the economy.
iwellemmeden-kel-dinnik.e: French forces occupied Tahoua and the surrounding region around 1900. [[e:tuareg|Tuareg]] uprisings during the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] were crushed by 1917, and the confederation was integrated into the [[s:colony-of-niger|Colony of Niger]] under French administration.

imamate-of-oman.t: The 20th-century Ibadi imamate of interior Oman, autonomous from the sultan of Muscat under the Treaty of Seeb until the Jebel Akhdar War.
imamate-of-oman.o: Interior tribes resented the coastal [[s:sultanate-of-muscat-and-oman|Sultanate of Muscat and Oman]], its British ties and its curbs on the arms trade. In 1913 Ibadi scholars and tribal leaders elected Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi as [[e:imam|imam]] at Tanuf; his forces took Nizwa and threatened [[e:muscat|Muscat]], which was saved by British Indian troops.
imamate-of-oman.r: The [[e:imamate|imamate]] revived the old Ibadi ideal of an elected [[e:imam|imam]] ruling by Islamic law, with Nizwa as capital and tribal leaders such as Isa ibn [[s:salihids|Salih]] al-Harthi as its strongmen. The Treaty of Seeb of 1920 gave the interior wide autonomy. Under Imam Muhammad al-Khalili, from 1920 to 1954, it remained isolated and conservative, with little trade or modern administration.
imamate-of-oman.e: After al-Khalili's death, [[e:imam|Imam]] Ghalib ibn Ali sought outside recognition as oil exploration began. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Said bin Taimur's forces, backed by [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], occupied Nizwa in 1955, and the Jebel Akhdar War ended in 1959 when British troops stormed the mountain. The leaders went into exile.

iroquois-confederacy.t: The Haudenosaunee league of five, later six, nations, bound by the Great Law of Peace and long the strongest Native power in north-eastern North America.
iroquois-confederacy.o: Haudenosaunee tradition tells how the Peacemaker, Deganawida, and his spokesman Hiawatha ended a time of blood feuds by persuading the [[s:mohawk-nation|Mohawk]], [[s:oneida-nation|Oneida]], [[s:onondaga-nation|Onondaga]], [[s:cayuga-nation|Cayuga]] and [[s:seneca-nation|Seneca]] to accept the Great Law of Peace, and by winning over the fearsome Onondaga chief Tadodaho. Dates proposed for the founding range from the 12th to the 16th century; the register follows a mid-15th-century date.
iroquois-confederacy.r: Fifty hereditary chiefs, chosen and removable by clan mothers, met in a [[e:grand-council-qing|Grand Council]] at [[s:onondaga-nation|Onondaga]], where the Onondaga kept the central fire and the wampum belts recording agreements. Decisions needed consensus. In the 17th-century Beaver Wars the league destroyed or scattered the [[s:huron-confederacy|Huron Confederacy]], the [[s:neutral-confederacy|Neutral Confederacy]] and the [[s:erie-nation|Erie Nation]], and through the Covenant Chain it became the main Native partner of the English colonies. The [[s:tuscarora-nation|Tuscarora]] joined around 1722, making Six Nations.
iroquois-confederacy.e: The American Revolution split the league: most nations sided with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], the [[s:oneida-nation|Oneida]] and [[s:tuscarora-nation|Tuscarora]] with the Americans. Joseph Brant led many to the Grand River in Ontario in 1784. The [[e:grand-council-qing|Grand Council]] still meets at [[s:onondaga-nation|Onondaga]] and at Six Nations of the Grand River.

cr.a: Rick Hill, Harold Johnson, and Tim Johnson

ilyasid-dynasty.t: A short-lived dynasty founded by a Samanid general that ruled the province of Kerman in south-eastern Iran for nearly forty years.
ilyasid-dynasty.o: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ilyas, a commander of Sogdian origin in the service of the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]], made himself master of [[e:kerman|Kerman]] around 932. He ruled from Bardasir, the forerunner of the modern city of Kerman, nominally recognising the [[e:samanid-empire|Samanids]].
ilyasid-dynasty.r: Muhammad ibn Ilyas held the province against the [[s:buyid-dynasty|Buyid dynasty]] and local tribes, including the Baluch and Qufs of the mountains. His rule was largely military, but [[e:kerman|Kerman's]] location between [[e:fars|Fars]], Sistan and Khurasan made it valuable for trade and tribute. Disputes between his sons, Alyasa and Ilyas, weakened the family after he retired.
ilyasid-dynasty.e: In 968 Adud al-Dawla of the [[s:buyid-dynasty|Buyids]] conquered [[e:kerman|Kerman]], ending the dynasty. Alyasa fled to Samanid territory.

isuwa.t: Isuwa, a Hurrian kingdom on the upper Euphrates, a buffer whose loyalty swung between the Hittites and Mitanni.
isuwa.o: Isuwa lay in the Elazığ plain, east of the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] in eastern [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], a region rich in [[e:copper|copper]]. It emerged as a kingdom by the 15th century BCE, inhabited by Hurrian-speaking people in the borderland between the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] and the [[s:mitanni-empire|Mitanni Empire]].
isuwa.r: Little is known of its government beyond Hittite treaties. Isuwa sheltered refugees from Hittite lands and often sided with [[e:mitanni|Mitanni]]. Salvage excavations before the Keban Dam flooded the plain uncovered fortified towns of the period.
isuwa.e: [[e:suppiluliuma-i|Suppiluliuma I]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] conquered Isuwa in the 14th century BCE and made it a [[e:vassal|vassal]]. After the Hittite collapse c. 1200 BCE, the region probably passed to the kingdom of [[s:melid|Melid]].

indonesia.t: The world's largest archipelagic state and most populous Muslim-majority country, independent since 1945.
indonesia.o: Indonesia was proclaimed by Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta on 17 August 1945, during the last days of the [[s:japanese-occupation-of-the-dutch-east-indies|Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies]]. Four years of revolution against returning [[e:dutch|Dutch]] forces followed, until the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] transferred [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] in December 1949 to the federal [[s:united-states-of-indonesia|United States of Indonesia]], which became a unitary republic in 1950.
indonesia.r: Sukarno replaced parliamentary democracy with Guided Democracy in 1959. After the failed coup of 1965 the army killed hundreds of thousands of alleged communists, and Suharto built the New Order, a military-backed regime that oversaw rapid growth, the invasion of [[s:east-timor|East Timor]] and widespread corruption. The state ideology of Pancasila unites some 280 million people of many faiths and languages.
indonesia.e: The Asian financial crisis forced Suharto to resign in 1998, and reforms brought free elections, regional autonomy, [[e:east-timor|East Timor's]] independence and peace in Aceh in 2005. Indonesia is now a G20 democracy building a new capital, Nusantara.

indore-state.t: The Maratha kingdom of the Holkars in Malwa, famed for the pious ruler Ahilyabai Holkar and later one of the leading princely states of central India.
indore-state.o: Malhar Rao Holkar, a shepherd's son who rose as a cavalry commander under [[e:peshwa|Peshwa]] [[e:baji-rao-i|Baji Rao I]], received lands in [[e:malwa|Malwa]] from about 1731. The [[e:holkars|Holkars]] became one of the main [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] houses; Ahilyabai later made Maheshwar on the Narmada their seat of government.
indore-state.r: Ahilyabai Holkar (ruled 1767–95) became renowned for just administration and for rebuilding temples and ghats across [[e:india|India]], from [[s:kingdom-of-kashi|Kashi]] to Somnath. Yashwant Rao Holkar fought the British in 1804–05, but after defeat at Mahidpur in 1817 the Treaty of Mandsaur made Indore a protected state, and the capital moved to Indore. The [[e:cotton|cotton]] trade made Indore a commercial city; Tukoji Rao III abdicated in 1926 after a murder scandal.
indore-state.e: Yashwant Rao Holkar II acceded to [[e:india|India]], and in 1948 Indore merged into [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]], joining Madhya Pradesh in 1956. Indore is now the state's largest city.

isle-de-france.t: French Mauritius, a naval base and plantation colony that threatened British India until its capture in 1810.
isle-de-france.o: [[e:france|France]] claimed Mauritius, abandoned by [[s:dutch-mauritius|Dutch Mauritius]] in 1710, in 1715 and renamed it Isle de France. Settlers arrived from [[s:ile-bourbon|Ile Bourbon]] in 1721, and under governor Mahe de La Bourdonnais from 1735 the colony was developed, with Port Louis built as a capital and naval harbour.
isle-de-france.r: Run first by the [[e:french-east-india-company|French East India Company]] and from 1767 by the crown, the colony relied on enslaved labour from Madagascar and [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Mozambique]] for [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and food production. The intendant Pierre Poivre introduced [[e:spice-trade|spices]] and created the Pamplemousses garden. During wars with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], corsairs such as Robert Surcouf raided British shipping from Port Louis.
isle-de-france.e: British forces captured the island in 1810, and the Treaty of [[e:paris|Paris]] of 1814 confirmed its cession along with the [[s:british-seychelles|Seychelles]]. Renamed Mauritius, it kept French law and language, and gained independence in 1968.

cr.a: David McSpadden from Daly City, United States

ibadi-imamate-of-tripolitania.t: The short-lived Ibadi imamate of Abu al-Khattab, which briefly ruled Tripoli and Kairouan before the Abbasids crushed it.
ibadi-imamate-of-tripolitania.o: Ibadi Kharijism, a moderate branch of Kharijite [[e:islam|Islam]] spread by missionaries from [[e:basra|Basra]], won many followers among the [[e:berbers|Berbers]] of [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]] and the Jebel Nafusa. In 757 they elected Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri as [[e:imam|imam]], and his forces took [[s:county-of-tripoli|Tripoli]] from the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate's]] local authorities.
ibadi-imamate-of-tripolitania.r: In 758 Abu al-Khattab captured [[e:kairouan|Kairouan]] from the Warfajuma, Sufri [[e:berbers|Berbers]] who had terrorised the city, and appointed Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam as its governor. The [[e:imamate|imamate]] rested on the support of Berber tribes such as the Hawwara and Nafusa and on the Ibadi ideal of an elected, pious ruler who could be deposed if he failed.
ibadi-imamate-of-tripolitania.e: In 761 an Abbasid army under Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath defeated and killed Abu al-Khattab near Tawargha. Ibn Rustam fled west and later founded the [[s:rustamid-imamate|Rustamid imamate]] at Tahert, carrying on the Ibadi state tradition.

ishkuza.t: A Scythian kingdom in north-western Iran that troubled and then allied with Assyria, remembered by Herodotus for a 28-year Scythian domination of Asia.
ishkuza.o: Scythian horsemen from the steppes north of the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]] entered the lands south of the Caucasus and around Lake Urmia in the early 7th century BCE. Assyrian texts of [[e:esarhaddon|Esarhaddon]] call their kingdom Ishkuza and name its leader Ishpakai, who was killed fighting [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] around 675 BCE.
ishkuza.r: The Ishkuza were [[e:mounted-archer|mounted archers]] who raided widely and sold their services to neighbouring powers. Their king Bartatua, identified with [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]]' Protothyes, sought an Assyrian princess in marriage, and the [[e:scythians|Scythians]] thereafter generally supported [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] against the [[e:medes|Medes]] and [[s:cimmerians|Cimmerians]]. Herodotus says that under Madyes, son of Protothyes, the Scythians defeated the Medes and dominated [[e:asia|Asia]] for 28 years. Their own institutions are known only through outsiders' reports.
ishkuza.e: According to [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]], the Median king [[e:cyaxares|Cyaxares]] killed the Scythian leaders at a banquet and drove them out, after which the [[s:median-empire|Median Empire]] absorbed their lands. The chronology of these events is uncertain.

injuid-dynasty.t: A short-lived dynasty that ruled Shiraz after the fall of the Ilkhans, whose ruler Abu Ishaq was the generous patron of the young Hafez.
injuid-dynasty.o: Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah was appointed by the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]] to manage the crown estates (inju) in [[e:fars|Fars]]. When the [[e:ilkhan|Ilkhan]] Abu Sa'id died in 1335, his family made itself master of [[e:shiraz|Shiraz]] and the province.
injuid-dynasty.r: The Injuids ruled a wealthy [[e:fars|Fars]] where poetry and [[e:sufism|Sufism]] flourished. Abu Ishaq Inju, who took power around 1343, was a cultivated and lavish ruler; [[e:ibn-battuta|Ibn Battuta]] visited his court, and Hafez and the satirist Ubayd Zakani praised him. He was also reckless, and his rivalry with the [[s:muzaffarid-dynasty|Muzaffarids]] of Yazd and [[e:kerman|Kerman]] drained his treasury.
injuid-dynasty.e: Mubariz al-Din Muhammad of the [[s:muzaffarid-dynasty|Muzaffarid dynasty]] took [[e:shiraz|Shiraz]] in 1353. Abu Ishaq fled to [[e:isfahan|Isfahan]], was captured and executed in 1357, ending the dynasty.

italian-republic-1802-1805.t: Napoleon's Italian Republic, the first state to bear the name Italy, governed for him from Milan by Francesco Melzi d'Eril.
italian-republic-1802-1805.o: At the Consulta of Lyon in January 1802, Italian delegates of the [[s:cisalpine-republic|Cisalpine Republic]] accepted a new constitution and elected [[e:napoleon|Napoleon Bonaparte]] as president. The republic was renamed Italian, a symbolic step for supporters of national unity.
italian-republic-1802-1805.r: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] ruled from [[e:paris|Paris]], while Vice-President Francesco Melzi d'Eril governed in [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]], building an efficient administration, reforming finances, introducing conscription and making a concordat with the [[e:papacy|papacy]] in 1803. [[e:milan|Milan's]] [[e:departement|departments]] and [[e:prefect|prefects]] followed the French model, and the republic's army fought in Napoleon's campaigns.
italian-republic-1802-1805.e: When [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] became emperor of the French, he turned the republic into the [[s:kingdom-of-italy-napoleonic|Kingdom of Italy (Napoleonic)]] in March 1805 and crowned himself king in [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]].

islamic-republic-of-pakistan.t: The Muslim-majority republic of South Asia, a nuclear power whose history has alternated between civilian and military rule.
islamic-republic-of-pakistan.o: [[e:pakistan|Pakistan's]] first constitution, adopted on 23 March 1956, ended the [[s:dominion-of-pakistan|Dominion of Pakistan]] and declared an Islamic republic with Iskander Mirza as president. It was abrogated in 1958 when Ayub Khan seized power. The capital moved from Karachi to the newly built city of Islamabad in the 1960s.
islamic-republic-of-pakistan.r: Military rulers, Ayub Khan, Yahya Khan, Zia-ul-Haq and Pervez Musharraf, governed for long periods, interspersed with civilian governments of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Benazir Bhutto and Nawaz Sharif. Zia promoted [[e:islamisation|Islamisation]] of law. [[e:pakistan|Pakistan]] fought wars with [[e:india|India]] over [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] and conducted nuclear tests in 1998. The 1973 constitution, still in force, created a parliamentary federation.
islamic-republic-of-pakistan.e: In 1971 [[s:bangladesh|East Pakistan]] seceded after a brutal war and became Bangladesh. The republic continues as a federal parliamentary state of four provinces and other territories, with the army a powerful political force.

italian-east-africa.t: Mussolini's short-lived East African empire, created after the conquest of Ethiopia and destroyed by British and Ethiopian forces in 1941.
italian-east-africa.o: [[e:italy|Italy]] invaded [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]] in October 1935, using aircraft and [[e:poison-gas|poison gas]], and captured [[e:addis-ababa|Addis Ababa]] in May 1936. Victor Emmanuel III was proclaimed Emperor of [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia]], and Ethiopia was merged with [[s:italian-eritrea|Italian Eritrea]] and [[s:italian-somaliland|Italian Somaliland]] to form Italian East Africa, governed by a [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] in Addis Ababa.
italian-east-africa.r: The empire was divided into [[e:governorate|governorates]]. Italian rule was harsh: after an attempt on [[e:viceroy-of-india|Viceroy]] Rodolfo Graziani's life in February 1937, thousands were massacred in [[e:addis-ababa|Addis Ababa]], and the monastery of Debre Libanos was attacked. [[e:italy|Italy]] built roads and planned settlement, but Ethiopian patriots, the arbegnoch, kept up resistance. In 1940 Italian forces occupied [[s:british-somaliland|British Somaliland]].
italian-east-africa.e: In 1941 British, Commonwealth and Ethiopian forces counter-attacked. [[e:haile-selassie|Haile Selassie]] re-entered [[e:addis-ababa|Addis Ababa]] on 5 May 1941, and the last Italian forces surrendered at Gondar in November. [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] and [[s:somalia|Somalia]] passed under British administration.

cr.a: F l a n k e r

illyrian-kingdom.t: Kingdom of the Illyrians on the eastern Adriatic, ruled at its height by Agron and Queen Teuta, whose piracy provoked Rome's first wars across the Adriatic.
illyrian-kingdom.o: Illyrian kingdoms appear from about 400 BCE, when Bardylis built a power that defeated [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]] in 393 and 359 BCE. In the 3rd century BCE the Ardiaean dynasty under Agron united the coast from the Neretva to Epirus, with Scodra (Shkodër) and Rhizon (Risan) as royal seats.
illyrian-kingdom.r: Kings ruled through tribal chiefs and depended on a strong fleet of light lembi, used for war and for raiding Adriatic and Ionian shipping. Agron defeated the Aetolians in 231 BCE. Royal coins were struck at Scodra and Lissus. Greek cities such as Pharos and Issa lay on its edges.
illyrian-kingdom.e: Teuta's attacks on Italian traders led to the First Illyrian War in 229 BCE, and Demetrius of Pharos provoked a second in 219 BCE. In the Third Illyrian War of 168 BCE [[e:rome|Rome]] captured King Gentius at Scodra and split the kingdom, which later became the province of Illyricum.

ilorin-emirate.t: A Yoruba-speaking emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate, born from a revolt against the Oyo Empire, whose rise helped bring about Oyo's collapse.
ilorin-emirate.o: [[e:ilorin|Ilorin]] was a frontier town of the [[s:oyo-empire|Oyo Empire]]. Around 1817 its commander [[e:afonja|Afonja]], holding the military title Are Ona Kakanfo, rebelled against the [[e:alaafin|Alaafin]], relying on the [[e:fula|Fulani]] cleric Shehu Alimi and [[e:hausa|Hausa]] and [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] Muslim fighters. After Alimi's death his son Abdulsalami turned on Afonja, killed him around 1823, and became the first emir under the [[s:gwandu-emirate|Gwandu Emirate]].
ilorin-emirate.r: [[e:ilorin|Ilorin's]] cavalry raided deep into Yorubaland and helped destroy the old [[e:oyo-empire|Oyo]] capital in the 1830s, but [[s:ibadan|Ibadan]] defeated it at Osogbo around 1840, halting the [[e:jihad|jihad]]'s advance south. The [[e:emirate|emirate]] combined [[e:fula|Fulani]] rulers, [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]], [[e:hausa|Hausa]] and [[e:nupe-kingdom|Nupe]] residents, and became a centre of Islamic learning, crafts such as pottery and weaving, and trade between the savanna and the forest.
ilorin-emirate.e: [[e:ilorin|Ilorin]] fought in the long [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] wars against the [[s:ekiti-parapo|Ekiti Parapo]]. In 1897 the [[s:royal-niger-company-territories|Royal Niger Company]] defeated [[e:emir|Emir]] Suleiman, and Ilorin passed to the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]]. Its emir still reigns in Kwara State.

ishiyama-hongan-ji.t: The fortified headquarters of the True Pure Land Buddhist sect at Osaka, which withstood Oda Nobunaga for ten years before surrendering in 1580.
ishiyama-hongan-ji.o: After its temple at Yamashina near [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] was burned by rival forces in 1532, the leadership of the Hongan-ji moved in 1533 to Ishiyama, a site on high ground at the mouth of the Yodo river, where a temple had been founded by Rennyo.
ishiyama-hongan-ji.r: Under the head priests Shonyo and Kennyo, Ishiyama became a moated fortress and temple town, supported by donations from believers across [[e:japan|Japan]] and by the Ikko leagues that controlled provinces such as Kaga. The abbot acted as a great lord, negotiating with warlords and the court, and the surrounding town grew into a commercial centre.
ishiyama-hongan-ji.e: From 1570 Kennyo fought [[e:oda-nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]], supplied by sea by the Mori navy until Nobunaga's iron-clad ships cut the route in 1578. Mediated by the emperor, Kennyo surrendered in 1580. Hideyoshi built [[e:osaka-castle|Osaka Castle]] on the site, and the Hongan-ji later split into two branches.

iberian-union.t: The 60 years in which Spain's Habsburg kings also ruled Portugal and its empire, bringing the whole Iberian Peninsula under one crown.
iberian-union.o: King [[e:sebastian-of-portugal|Sebastian of Portugal]] died without heirs at Alcácer Quibir in [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] in 1578, and his successor, the elderly Cardinal Henry, died in 1580. [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II of Spain]] pressed his claim, won the Battle of Alcântara and was recognised as Philip I of Portugal by the Cortes of Tomar in 1581.
iberian-union.r: It was a personal union: Portugal kept its own laws, Cortes, currency and colonial administration, governed by a [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] and the Council of Portugal. But union drew Portugal into [[e:spain|Spain's]] wars, and the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] attacked [[s:colonial-brazil|Portuguese Brazil]], [[e:africa|Africa]] and [[e:asia|Asia]]. The Count-Duke of Olivares's plans for tax and military integration caused growing resentment.
iberian-union.e: On 1 December 1640 Portuguese nobles rose in [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] and proclaimed the Duke of Braganza as John IV. The Restoration War ended with Spanish recognition of Portuguese independence in the Treaty of Lisbon of 1668.

imperial-abbey-of-irsee.t: Benedictine abbey in the Allgäu that gained immediacy late and became known for its scholarship in science and mathematics.
imperial-abbey-of-irsee.o: Irsee Abbey was founded around 1182 by the margraves of Ronsberg as a Benedictine monastery near [[s:free-imperial-city-of-kaufbeuren|Kaufbeuren]]. Over the centuries the abbots expanded their rights, and in 1692 the abbey bought the jurisdiction and was recognised as an imperial abbey, immediate to the Empire.
imperial-abbey-of-irsee.r: The abbot ruled a small territory of villages as a prelate of the Empire, with a seat on the Swabian bench of prelates. The monks rebuilt the abbey in baroque style and maintained a school and a respected natural sciences cabinet; Ulrich Weiss, a monk of Irsee, was a noted philosopher and mathematician of the Catholic [[e:age-of-enlightenment|Enlightenment]].
imperial-abbey-of-irsee.e: The abbey was secularised in 1802 and its lands given to the [[s:electorate-of-bavaria|Electorate of Bavaria]]. The buildings later served as an asylum, whose patients were victims of Nazi euthanasia killings, and are now a conference centre.

imperial-abbey-of-engelberg.t: A Benedictine abbey in a high valley of central Switzerland that ruled the valley as a tiny state until 1798 and still flourishes today.
imperial-abbey-of-engelberg.o: Conrad of Sellenbüren founded the Benedictine abbey of Engelberg in 1120 in a remote valley below Mount Titlis, with monks from Muri. In 1124 [[e:papacy|Pope]] Calixtus II and Emperor Henry V confirmed its foundation and imperial protection, making it a free imperial abbey.
imperial-abbey-of-engelberg.r: The abbots ruled the Engelberg valley as lords, with rights of justice over its farmers. Under Abbot Frowin in the 12th century the abbey had a notable scriptorium. Engelberg was protected by the Swiss cantons of [[s:canton-of-lucerne|Lucerne]], [[s:canton-of-schwyz|Schwyz]], [[s:canton-of-unterwalden|Unterwalden]] and Uri, and dairying and cheese provided its income.
imperial-abbey-of-engelberg.e: French invasion in 1798 ended the abbey's secular rule, and the valley was incorporated into the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. In 1815 it joined the canton of Obwalden. The monastery survives as an active Benedictine community, and Engelberg is now a resort.

ishaqid-dynasty.t: A Sunni dynasty that ruled western Gilan on the Caspian coast from Fuman until Shah Abbas I absorbed it.
ishaqid-dynasty.o: [[e:gilan|Gilan]] was divided by the Sefidrud river into Biyapas, west of the river, and Biyapish to the east. From around the 14th century the Ishaqids, who claimed descent from the prophet Isaac, ruled Biyapas, with their centres at Fuman and later Rasht.
ishaqid-dynasty.r: The Ishaqids were [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] of the [[e:shafii-school|Shafi'i school]], unlike their eastern rivals the [[s:karkiya-dynasty|Karkiya dynasty]], who were Zaydi and later Twelver [[e:shia-islam|Shia]]; wars between the two halves of [[e:gilan|Gilan]] were frequent. The economy rested on [[e:rice|rice]], [[e:silk|silk]] and fishing, and Gilan's silk became valuable to the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]]. Amira Dubbaj, a ruler of the early 16th century, married into the Safavid family before rebelling.
ishaqid-dynasty.e: [[e:abbas-i-of-persia|Shah Abbas I]] conquered [[e:gilan|Gilan]] in 1592, removing the last Ishaqid ruler, Jamshid Khan, and making the province, with its [[e:silk|silk]], crown land.

igala-kingdom.t: Kingdom at the confluence of the Niger and Benue, ruled by the Attah of Igala from Idah and a rival of Benin in the 16th century.
igala-kingdom.o: The [[e:igala|Igala]] kingdom took shape on the east bank of the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] below its confluence with the Benue, probably by the 15th century. Its traditions point to links with both the Jukun of [[s:kwararafa|Kwararafa]] and the [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] and [[e:benin-empire|Benin]] worlds, and the royal dynasty is associated with Ayegba om'Idoko, a celebrated early Attah.
igala-kingdom.r: The Attah was a sacred king, surrounded by a council of kingmakers, the [[e:igala|Igala]] Mela, who represented the older clans. Controlling river traffic, Igala traded in slaves, cloth and salt, and its influence reached into northern Igboland around Nsukka. In the early 16th century Igala fought a major war with the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]], which ended in [[e:benin-empire|Benin's]] favour.
igala-kingdom.e: In the 19th century European traders and missionaries reached Idah by river, and the [[s:royal-niger-company-territories|Royal Niger Company]] set up stations nearby. [[e:igala|Igala]] came under British rule around 1900 and was included in [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Northern Nigeria]]. The Attah still reigns at Idah in Kogi State.

ifni.t: A small Spanish enclave on Morocco's Atlantic coast, occupied only in 1934, fought over in the Ifni War and returned to Morocco in 1969.
ifni.o: In the Treaty of Wad [[e:ras|Ras]] of 1860, ending the Hispano-Moroccan War, [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] ceded [[e:spain|Spain]] a coastal territory identified with the medieval post of Santa Cruz de Mar Pequeña. Its location was disputed for decades, and Spain occupied Sidi Ifni only in 1934.
ifni.r: Ifni was a small military colony with a garrison town, Sidi Ifni, built in Spanish style, ruling Ait Ba Amran [[e:berbers|Berber]] tribes of the hinterland. From 1946 it formed part of [[s:spanish-sahara|Spanish West Africa]] with Spanish [[e:sahara|Sahara]]. It had little economic value beyond fishing.
ifni.e: In 1957 to 1958 Moroccan irregulars of the Army of Liberation attacked in the Ifni War, confining [[e:spain|Spain]] to the town itself, which became a Spanish province in 1958. Under UN pressure, Spain handed Ifni to the [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Kingdom of Morocco]] in June 1969.

iverni.t: People of south-west Ireland named by Ptolemy, whose name is linked to the Érainn and to Ériu, the Irish name for Ireland itself.
iverni.o: Ptolemy's Geography of about 150 places the Iverni in the south-west of Ireland, around modern Cork, with a town called Ivernis and a river Iernus nearby. Their name is related to Ivernia or Hibernia, the classical name for the island, and to the Érainn, a population group prominent in the early genealogies of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]].
iverni.r: Classical sources record nothing of their rulers or customs. Early Irish tradition remembers the Érainn as an ancient people of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]], ancestors of groups such as the [[s:corcu-loigde|Corcu Loigde]] and the Corcu Duibne, who were powerful before the rise of the Eóganachta. The region has many ogham stones, the earliest Irish writing.
iverni.e: By the early medieval period the Érainn had been eclipsed by the Eóganachta, who built the [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Kingdom of Munster]] around Cashel. Érainn descendants such as the [[s:corcu-loigde|Corcu Loigde]] survived as subordinate kingdoms in west Cork.

ilansura.t: Ilansura, a small kingdom of the Khabur region best known for the unhappy marriage of King Haya-Sumu to two daughters of Zimri-Lim of Mari.
ilansura.o: Ilansura was a city of the Ida-Maras district in north-eastern [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] whose exact site has not been identified. It emerged as an independent kingdom after the death of Shamshi-Adad and the break-up of the [[s:kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia|Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia]] in the 1770s BCE.
ilansura.r: Its king Haya-Sumu was a close ally of [[e:zimri-lim|Zimri-Lim]] of [[s:mari|Mari]], who gave him his daughters Shimatum and Kirum in marriage. Kirum's letters to her father, complaining of humiliation by her sister and pleading to come home, are among the most personal documents of the [[e:mari|Mari]] archive.
ilansura.e: After [[s:mari|Mari]] was destroyed by the [[s:babylonian-empire|Babylonian Empire]] c. 1760 BCE, Ilansura disappears from the record.

iar-connacht.t: The O'Flaherty lordship of Connemara and western Galway, whose rulers' raids, by tradition, led Galway city to pray for deliverance 'from the ferocious O'Flahertys'.
iar-connacht.o: The O'Flahertys were originally kings of Muintir Murchada east of Lough Corrib. Driven westwards by the Anglo-Norman de Burghs in the 13th century, they established themselves in Iar [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Connacht]], the land west of Lough Corrib including Connemara.
iar-connacht.r: The O'Flahertys ruled a rugged land of bogs, mountains and sea, raising [[e:cattle|cattle]] and fishing, and building tower houses such as Aughnanure. Their [[e:galley|galleys]], like those of Grace O'Malley, who married Donal O'Flaherty, controlled the coast. They were frequently at war with the merchant town of Galway.
iar-connacht.e: The Composition of [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Connacht]] in 1585 converted Gaelic lordship into English tenure, and Sir Murrough O'Flaherty submitted to the crown. The family lost most of its estates in the Cromwellian confiscations of the 1650s.

imperial-abbey-of-kornelimunster.t: A Carolingian abbey near Aachen, founded by Louis the Pious for the reformer Benedict of Aniane, which ruled a tiny imperial territory until 1802.
imperial-abbey-of-kornelimunster.o: In 814 Emperor [[e:louis-the-pious|Louis the Pious]] founded a monastery at Inda, near his palace at [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]], for Benedict of Aniane, the leading reformer of Frankish monasticism. In 817 a council held at [[e:aachen|Aachen]] imposed the Benedictine Rule on all monasteries of the empire, with Inda as a model house.
imperial-abbey-of-kornelimunster.r: The abbey received relics of [[e:papacy|Pope]] Cornelius in 875, and the place became known as Kornelimünster. Its abbots were princes of the Empire ruling a small territory, the Münsterländchen, of a few villages. Relics presented to the faithful included textiles believed to be from the Passion of Christ, shown every seven years in the [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]] pilgrimage.
imperial-abbey-of-kornelimunster.e: The French annexed the area in 1794 and dissolved the abbey in 1802. The territory passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815. The former abbey buildings later housed a collection of modern art, and the church continues as a parish church.

imperial-abbey-of-elchingen.t: A Benedictine abbey above the Danube near Ulm whose abbots ruled a small territory, and which gave its name to Napoleon's battle of 1805.
imperial-abbey-of-elchingen.o: The abbey was founded on a hill above the [[e:danube|Danube]] in the early 12th century by local nobles related to the Hohenstaufen and settled by Benedictine monks. The [[s:free-imperial-city-of-ulm|Free Imperial City of Ulm]] held its advocacy for long periods, and the abbey achieved full imperial status at the end of the 15th century.
imperial-abbey-of-elchingen.r: The abbot governed several villages as a member of the Swabian Circle and of the Swabian bench of prelates. Disputes with Ulm, whose Protestant territory surrounded the abbey, were frequent. Elchingen remained Catholic and in the 18th century rebuilt its church in late Baroque and early neoclassical style.
imperial-abbey-of-elchingen.e: The abbey was secularised in 1802 and given to Bavaria. On 14 October 1805 Marshal Ney defeated an Austrian force at the Battle of Elchingen during the Ulm campaign and was later made Duke of Elchingen. The abbey church survives in Oberelchingen.

imperial-abbey-of-thorn.t: A tiny principality on the Maas ruled by an abbess and her chapter of noble canonesses, an imperial estate for five centuries.
imperial-abbey-of-thorn.o: The abbey was founded around 990 by Count Ansfried, later [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]], and his wife Hilsondis, with their daughter Benedicta as first abbess. It became a house of secular canonesses drawn from high-born families, and the register dates its status as an immediate imperial territory, with the abbess a princess of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]], to 1292.
imperial-abbey-of-thorn.r: The princess-abbess ruled the village of Thorn and a few surrounding hamlets with her chapter of noble ladies, who were not bound by permanent vows and could leave to marry. The abbey kept its own courts and belonged to the Lower Rhenish–Westphalian Circle of the Empire. Its white-painted village remains well preserved.
imperial-abbey-of-thorn.e: French revolutionary troops occupied the area in 1794 and the chapter fled; the principality was abolished and its lands annexed to [[e:france|France]]. The last abbess was Maria Kunigunde of Saxony. Thorn later became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Kingdom of the Netherlands]].

italian-republic.t: Modern Italy, a democratic republic since the referendum of 1946 and a founding member of the European Communities and NATO.
italian-republic.o: On 2 June 1946 Italians voted in a referendum to abolish the monarchy of the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]], and Enrico De Nicola became provisional head of state. A Constituent Assembly drafted a new constitution, which came into force on 1 January 1948.
italian-republic.r: [[e:italy|Italy]] is a parliamentary republic with a president as head of state. Christian Democrat governments led by Alcide De Gasperi and his successors anchored it in NATO in 1949 and the European Economic Community, founded by the Treaty of [[e:rome|Rome]] in 1957. The economic miracle of the 1950s and 1960s transformed the country, though it suffered political terrorism in the Years of Lead and a lasting gap between north and south.
italian-republic.e: The Tangentopoli corruption scandals of 1992 swept away the old party system. [[e:italy|Italy]] adopted the euro in 1999 and remains a major European economy; Sergio Mattarella has been president since 2015.

isaaq-sultanate.t: A sultanate of the Isaaq clans of northern Somalia whose sultans mediated clan affairs from Toon until the British protectorate.
isaaq-sultanate.o: According to tradition the Isaaq clans chose a common sultan in the mid-18th century after a victory over rival clans at the battle of Lafaruug. Guled Abdi of the Eidagale became the first sultan, and his descendants, the Rer Guled, held the title, with their seat at Toon near Hargeisa.
isaaq-sultanate.r: The sultan was a mediator and war leader rather than an absolute ruler, presiding over councils of elders who applied [[e:somalis|Somali]] customary law, xeer, and Islamic law. The Isaaq economy rested on [[e:camel|camel]] and sheep herding and on trade through Berbera, whose annual fair drew merchants from [[e:arabia|Arabia]] and [[e:india|India]].
isaaq-sultanate.e: Between 1884 and 1886 Isaaq clans signed treaties with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], and their lands became part of [[s:british-somaliland|British Somaliland]]. Some Isaaq branches had their own sultans, such as the [[s:habr-yunis-sultanate|Habr Yunis Sultanate]]. The Isaaq heartland is today the core of the [[s:republic-of-somaliland|Republic of Somaliland]].

italian-somaliland.t: Italy's colony in southern and north-eastern Somalia, the launch pad for the invasion of Ethiopia in 1935 and later part of Italian East Africa.
italian-somaliland.o: In 1888 and 1889 [[e:italy|Italy]] made [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] treaties with the [[s:sultanate-of-hobyo|Sultanate of Hobyo]] and the [[s:majeerteen-sultanate|Majeerteen Sultanate]]. In 1892 it leased the Benadir ports, including [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]], Merca and [[s:barawa|Barawa]], from the [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Sultanate of Zanzibar]], administering them at first through [[e:chartered-company|chartered companies]]. The Italian state took direct control in 1905 and bought the ports outright.
italian-somaliland.r: Italian rule spread slowly inland. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] ceded Jubaland in 1924 and under the Fascist governor Cesare De Vecchi the northern sultanates were conquered by 1927. Italian concessions developed banana and [[e:cotton|cotton]] plantations along the Shabelle and Jubba rivers, often with forced labour. [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]] gained Italian-style buildings, among them a cathedral, now destroyed.
italian-somaliland.e: The Walwal incident of 1934 became [[e:italy|Italy's]] pretext for invading [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]], and in 1936 the colony became part of [[s:italian-east-africa|Italian East Africa]]. British forces occupied it in 1941. In 1950 Italy returned as administrator of the UN [[s:trust-territory-of-somaliland|Trust Territory of Somaliland]].

iazyges.t: Sarmatian horse nomads who settled the plain between the Danube and Tisza and fought Marcus Aurelius before becoming Roman auxiliaries.
iazyges.o: The Iazyges were a Sarmatian people of the steppe north of the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]]. In the first half of the 1st century CE they moved west into the plain between the [[e:danube|Danube]] and Tisza in modern [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and [[s:serbia|Serbia]], wedging themselves between Roman [[e:pannonia|Pannonia]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-dacia|Kingdom of Dacia]].
iazyges.r: They were mounted pastoralists led by kings and nobles, famed for armoured [[e:lance|lancers]]. [[e:rome|Rome]] alternately paid and fought them, using them against the Dacians. In the Marcomannic Wars they invaded [[e:pannonia|Pannonia]]; after defeat on the frozen [[e:danube|Danube]], King Zanticus made peace with Marcus Aurelius in 175 CE and sent 8,000 cavalry, many of them posted to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]].
iazyges.e: They remained a troublesome neighbour, fighting Constantine and [[e:constantius-ii|Constantius II]] in the 4th century. The arrival of the [[e:huns|Huns]] around 375 overwhelmed them, and they were absorbed into the Hunnic sphere and later peoples of the Carpathian basin.

iskolat.t: Soviet government of unoccupied Latvia in 1917-1918, backed by the Latvian Riflemen, the first Latvian soviet state.
iskolat.o: After the Bolshevik seizure of power in [[e:petrograd|Petrograd]] in November 1917, Latvian Bolsheviks, strongly supported by the Latvian Riflemen, formed the Executive Committee of the Soviet of Workers, Soldiers and Landless of [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]], known by its Russian acronym Iskolat. It governed the part of Latvia not occupied by [[e:germany|Germany]], with its seat in Valka and later Cēsis.
iskolat.r: Iskolat declared the land of the Baltic German manors nationalised, introduced eight-hour working days and organised local soviets. It worked closely with Lenin's government in [[e:petrograd|Petrograd]] but had little time to build institutions, and Latvian nationalists rejected it as illegitimate.
iskolat.e: In February 1918 the German army advanced in Operation Faustschlag and occupied all of [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]], and Iskolat fled to [[e:russia|Russia]]. Its leaders later formed the [[s:latvian-socialist-soviet-republic|Latvian Socialist Soviet Republic]] in December 1918, while nationalists proclaimed the Republic of Latvia.

italian-eritrea.t: Italy's first colony, carved from the Red Sea coast and highlands, which gave Eritrea its borders, its capital Asmara and a distinct identity.
italian-eritrea.o: An Italian shipping company bought the port of [[e:assab-bay|Assab]] in 1869, and the Italian state took it over in 1882. [[e:italy|Italy]] occupied [[e:massawa|Massawa]] in 1885 with British approval and pushed inland, despite defeat at Dogali in 1887. The Treaty of Wuchale with [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik II]] in 1889 recognised its gains, and on 1 January 1890 the colony of [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] was proclaimed.
italian-eritrea.r: [[e:italy|Italy's]] defeat at [[e:battle-of-adwa|Adwa]] in 1896 fixed the border with [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]]. Under governors such as Ferdinando Martini, the capital moved to Asmara, which was rebuilt with Italian modernist architecture. A railway linked [[e:massawa|Massawa]] to Asmara and Agordat, and tens of thousands of Eritrean askari served in Italy's colonial wars. [[e:racial-segregation|Racial segregation]] was imposed under [[e:fascism|Fascism]].
italian-eritrea.e: In 1936 [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] became part of [[s:italian-east-africa|Italian East Africa]]. British forces took it in 1941 after the Battle of Keren, beginning the [[s:british-administration-of-eritrea|British Administration of Eritrea]]. Asmara's Italian-era centre is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

imperial-abbey-of-rot-an-der-rot.t: A Premonstratensian abbey in upper Swabia, the order's first house in the region, whose abbots ruled a small imperial territory.
imperial-abbey-of-rot-an-der-rot.o: Founded around 1126 by Premonstratensian canons, Rot was the first house of the order in Swabia. Its lands grew through gifts from local nobles, and in 1376 [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]] confirmed its direct dependence on the empire, freeing it from outside advocates.
imperial-abbey-of-rot-an-der-rot.r: The abbot governed several villages in the Rot valley as a member of the Swabian Circle and of the Swabian bench of prelates in the [[e:imperial-diet|Imperial Diet]]. The abbey's income came from farms, forests and tithes. It remained Catholic and in the 18th century rebuilt its church of Saint Verena in late Baroque style.
imperial-abbey-of-rot-an-der-rot.e: In 1803 the abbey was secularised and given to the counts of Wartenberg as compensation, and in 1806 it passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-wurttemberg|Kingdom of Württemberg]]. The church and abbey buildings survive in Rot an der Rot.

imperial-abbey-of-kaisheim.t: Wealthy Cistercian abbey near Donauwörth whose abbots won immediacy within the Empire and ruled villages across Swabia.
imperial-abbey-of-kaisheim.o: Kaisheim Abbey was founded in 1133 by Count Henry of Lechsgemünd and settled by Cistercian monks. It gained imperial protection early, but its status was disputed for centuries with the dukes of Bavaria and the counts of [[s:county-of-oettingen|Oettingen]], until its immediacy was recognised in 1656.
imperial-abbey-of-kaisheim.r: The abbot ruled as a prelate of the Empire, sitting on the Swabian bench of prelates in the [[e:imperial-diet|Imperial Diet]]. The abbey held lands, villages and town houses around the [[e:danube|Danube]] and Lech, collecting rents and tithes. It built a large baroque complex at Kaisheim and was known for its library and its imperial hall, the Kaisersaal.
imperial-abbey-of-kaisheim.e: In the secularisation of 1802 and 1803 the abbey was dissolved and its lands given to the [[s:electorate-of-bavaria|Electorate of Bavaria]]. The buildings became a prison, which they still house today.

italian-libya.t: Italy's North African colony, conquered from the Ottomans and subdued by a brutal war, which Mussolini made a settler province before its loss in 1943.
italian-libya.o: [[e:italy|Italy]] invaded the [[s:tripolitania-vilayet|Tripolitania Vilayet]] in 1911 and, by the Treaty of Ouchy in 1912, obtained [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]] and [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] from the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. Resistance confined Italian control to the coast, especially during the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], when the [[s:senussi-order|Senussi Order]] and the [[s:tripolitanian-republic|Tripolitanian Republic]] held the interior.
italian-libya.r: From 1922 Fascist [[e:italy|Italy]] reconquered the interior. In [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]], Rodolfo Graziani deported much of the nomadic population into [[e:concentration-camp|concentration camps]] where tens of thousands died, and Omar al-Mukhtar was hanged in 1931. The two colonies were united as [[e:libya|Libya]] in 1934. Governor Italo Balbo built the coastal road and settled some 20,000 Italian farmers in 1938.
italian-libya.e: During the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]], British Commonwealth forces captured [[s:county-of-tripoli|Tripoli]] in January 1943, ending Italian rule. [[e:italy|Italy]] renounced [[e:libya|Libya]] in 1947, and the country came under the [[s:british-military-administration-of-libya|British Military Administration of Libya]] and the [[s:fezzan-ghadames-military-territory|Fezzan-Ghadames Military Territory]].
